ut_san_rafael_swell_north.blurb: The northern San Rafael Swell is remote desert country north of I-70, with climbing scattered over a wide area rather than packed into one cluster. Buckhorn Wash is the heart of it, a deep sandstone canyon whose walls expose several sandstone formations. Most lines follow cracks and are trad, with newer sport routes on faces that offer enough features, and the whole place is far quieter than Moab or Indian Creek. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, centred on 5.9 to 5.11, and there is a small amount of bouldering and aid. Beyond the wash, Mexican Mountain Road Area and The Weasel Formation hold smaller collections of climbs.

md_sugarloaf_mountain.blurb: Sugarloaf is a small wooded monadnock of roughly 1,200 feet, and the rock is white quartzite that can be sharp on ropes and hands. Bouldering makes up more than half the climbing, mostly V0 to V4 with a few harder problems, and the remainder is trad and top-rope. Roped grades range widely, from easy fives up to 5.12, with the greatest share in the 5.6 to 5.10 range. Crags worth knowing include Devil's Kitchen, Middle Earth and White Rocks, and the main boulder groups are Peak Talus Boulders and Southern Spur Boulders. Most areas sit under trees, which gives summer shade, but the rock can stay wet for a day or two after rain.

az_oak_flat.blurb: Oak Flat is the bouldering zone of Queen Creek Canyon, near Superior and about an hour east of Phoenix. The boulders are volcanic and can be abrasive, but they offer a wide variety of holds, and the problems range from delicate slabs to steep, dynamic highballs. Nearly everything here is bouldering. Easy problems are plentiful, with V0 the most common grade, a good spread through V1 to V5, and a smaller number of hard problems above that. The ground is broken into many small zones, including Entrance Boulders, Atlantis #2, Hidden World South and Davey Jones Locker, and the cliffs of the canyon around it are welded volcanic tuff.

ny_a_lake_champlain_region.blurb: This stretch of the Adirondacks reaches toward Lake Champlain, with most crags in the park between Route 9 and I-87 and the densest cluster along the Northway. Trad is the main style, followed by sport, with a modest amount of winter ice and a little bouldering. Poke-O-Moonshine is the big one, with multi-pitch climbs up to 500 feet, steep cracks and ice columns in winter, while Deadwater is mostly single-pitch and leans sport. Rock grades run from about 5.4 to 5.13, with the largest share between 5.9 and 5.12, and the ice sits mostly in WI4 and WI5. The region mixes a few large cliffs with many small crags along the highway.

or_cline_falls.blurb: Cline Falls is a small basalt crag along the Deschutes River, minutes west of Redmond, in a rimrock canyon with juniper and ponderosa pine above. Bouldering dominates by a wide margin, with problems from V0 to V10 and most of them at V0 to V4. A few short roped climbs, trad, sport and top-rope, mostly 5.9 and up, sit on the cliffs below the falls. The boulders are spread through zones along the river, and the route cliff on the west-facing side stays shaded in summer until about three in the afternoon. When the river runs higher in fall and winter, getting to the boulders can be harder.

pa_governor_dick_park_aka_mount_gretna.blurb: Governor Dick Park, also called Mount Gretna, is a bouldering area in south-central Pennsylvania. Diabase boulders sit in groups through dense forest, and every climb here is a boulder problem. Grades start at the very easiest and stretch to about V11, with the heart of the range between V0 and V7 and a respectable handful of harder ones. The boulders are only minutes apart once you know the layout, which makes it a good place for circuits and training, though finding your way around without a guide can be tricky. Colflesh Area, Shamu Area, 45 Area and Highball Area are among the largest zones. Fall and spring are the best seasons; summer brings humidity, ticks, flies and thick underbrush.
